notes: The conditional derivation of N004 is valid from N001 and N002. It preserves the singleton-enlargement route and requires only the routine mathematical completions recorded below. No external E applications occur.

applicability.notes: N001 is instantiated with m=n, A=E, s=q; N002 and L2 give q>D≥0, and L3 gives a positive scale. The metric-ball fact uses L1 (n≥1); power and series facts use q>0 and ε,r>0. No measurability or source-paper fact is invoked.

argument.notes: H^q(E)=0 forces H^q_r(E)=0 and supplies F001 with cost <ε/2. Every nonempty zero-diameter member is a singleton; its replacement contains it and has diameter d_i in (0,r]. Unchanged members retain their bounds. The nonnegative cost comparison gives total cost at most the original cost plus ε/4, hence <3ε/4<ε. This also covers an empty index set. All required covering and diameter clauses follow.

Other clauses of N002 are unnecessary here.

background_notes.fact: For q>0,r>0, H^q(E)=0 implies H^q_r(E)=0. If this scale content is zero, then for every η>0 there is an admissible countable cover with total q-cost <η; such a cover can be indexed by ℕ by inserting empty members without changing its cost or coverage.

grounds.reason: Scale content is the infimum of nonnegative countable-cover costs; measure is the supremum over positive scales, and empty sets cost zero.
N001 and N002 with L2–L4 give q>0, r>0, H^q(E)=0 and η=ε/2>0.

background_notes.justification: Each nonnegative scale content is bounded above by the zero supremum. If all admissible costs were at least η, their infimum would be at least η, contradicting zero; an empty admissible class has infimum ∞ and is excluded too. A countable family can be enumerated or placed at distinct natural indices; fill unused indices with empty sets. Reindexing nonnegative sums and adding zero terms preserves the cost.

background_notes.fact: A nonempty subset of a metric space with diameter zero is a singleton. For n≥1, x∈ℝ^n and d>0, the open ball B(x,d/2) contains x and has diameter exactly d.

grounds.reason: The diameter is the supremum of pairwise distances in the supplied Euclidean metric.
K consists of the nonempty W_i; each d_i is positive and finite, as justified by BG003.

background_notes.justification: Every pairwise distance in a zero-diameter set is zero, so metric separation identifies all its points with any selected member. In the ball, the triangle inequality bounds all pairwise distances by d. A first-coordinate unit vector e exists because n≥1. For 0<t<d/2 the points x±te lie in the ball and have distance 2t. These distances approach d as t increases to d/2, giving the reverse supremum bound; equality is of the supremum and does not require an attained pair.

background_notes.fact: For q,r,ε>0 and i∈ℕ, d_i=min(r,(ε·2^(-i-3))^(1/q)) is positive, is at most r, and satisfies d_i^q≤ε·2^(-i-3).

grounds.reason: L2, N002, L3 and L4 establish q,r,ε>0.
This is the definition of d_i for i∈K⊆ℕ.

background_notes.justification: Both entries of the minimum are positive finite reals. On positive reals the map t↦t^q is increasing for q>0 and ((a)^(1/q))^q=a. These power identities follow from t^u=exp(u log t), the inverse identities for exp and log, and their strict monotonicity. Apply this with a=ε·2^(-i-3)>0 and d_i≤a^(1/q).

background_notes.fact: For ε>0, sum_{i=0}^∞ ε·2^(-i-3)=ε/4. If original nonnegative costs a_i have sum A<ε/2, and modified costs on K⊆ℕ satisfy b_i≤a_i+ε·2^(-i-3), then sum_{i∈K} b_i≤A+ε/4<ε.

grounds.reason: Unchanged members have b_i=a_i, singleton originals have a_i=0 and replacement b_i=d_i^q≤ε·2^(-i-3); K⊆ℕ.

background_notes.justification: The partial sum through M is ε/4·(1-2^(-(M+1))), tending to ε/4 since 2^(-(M+1))→0. For any finite J⊆K, summing the pointwise bound gives sum_J b_i≤sum_J a_i+sum_J ε·2^(-i-3)≤A+ε/4. Taking the supremum over finite J, the definition of the nonnegative series, gives the claimed infinite-sum bound without any exchange of limits. Finally A+ε/4<3ε/4<ε.
